newsitem.title: CAMEROON: U.N. starts assessment of Nigeria-Cameroon row.
newsitem.headline: U.N. starts assessment of Nigeria-Cameroon row.

text.p: A U.N. fact-finding mission met Cameroon's Foreign Minister Ferdinand Leopold Oyono on Monday to try to ease border tension between Nigeria and Cameroon.
Government officials said the four-man mission headed by Indonesian Omar Alim also held talks with junior presidency minister Edourd Akame. There were no details of either talks.

Alim, who was scheduled to meet President Paul Biya later, tried to play down high expectations of the mission, which was prompted by clashes between Nigerian and Cameroonian troops over their disputed Bakassi peninsula border area.

"The mission has a limited goal," Alim told reporters in the Cameroon capital on Sunday night. "It consists essentially of reducing tension in the Bakassi region and determining the willingness of the two countries to abide by the ruling of the International Court of Justice in The Hague."
The mission is the most serious on-the-spot attempt to end the row that has brought the two countries to the brink of war.
A meeting was scheduled with Justice Minister Douala Moutome, who is in charge of Cameroon's case at the World Court, before talks with Biya and a visit to Bakassi and Nigeria.
Cameroon took the case to the court in 1994 but its ruling in March forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later resulting in casualties on both sides.
The dispute centres on agreements between former British and German colonisers in Bakassi, a string of small islands in the Gulf of Guinea believed to be rich in oil.
Prior to the U.N. initiative, Nigeria had always maintained that the dispute should be settled within the Lake Chad Commission which links Nigeria with Chad and Cameroon.
Nigerian officials said the U.N. team would spend Tuesday in Bakassi before heading for talks with Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha in Abuja on Wednesday.
They are also expected to visit Togo to meet President Gnassingbe Eyadema who is mediating on behalf of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
Nigerian and Cameroonian troops have clashed over the Bakassi peninsula since February 1994 and the two countries accuse each other of massing forces in the area.
Military sources said both sides wanted to maintain a strong position on the ground to help their claims in the final verdict of the World Court.
